segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ מִן הַכְּרוּב — אָסוּר בְּאִיסְפַּרְגוֹס, מִן הָאִיסְפַּרְגוֹס — מוּתָּר בִּכְרוּב.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» One who vows that «cabbage» is forbidden «to» him «is prohibited from» eating «ispargus,» as that is a type of cabbage. However, one who vows that «ispargus» is forbidden «to» him is «permitted to» eat «cabbage.»

segments.he: מִן הַגְּרִיסִין — אָסוּר בְּמִקְפָּה, וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי מַתִּיר. מִן הַמִּקְפָּה — מוּתָּר בִּגְרִיסִין. מִן הַמִּקְפָּה — אָסוּר בִּשּׁוּם, וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי מַתִּיר. מִן הַשּׁוּם — מוּתָּר בְּמִקְפָּה.
segments.en: One who vows that «pounded beans» are forbidden «to» him «is prohibited from» eating pounded bean «stew [mikpa]. However, Rabbi Yosei» rules that he is «permitted» to eat it. One who vows that pounded bean «stew» is forbidden «to» him is «permitted to» eat «pounded beans» according to all opinions. One who vows that «stew» is forbidden «to» him «is prohibited from» eating the «garlic» of the stew. «However, Rabbi Yosei» rules that he is «permitted» to eat the garlic. One who vows that «garlic» is forbidden «to» him «is permitted to» eat «stew.»

segments.he: מִן הָעֲדָשִׁים — אָסוּר בַּאֲשִׁישִׁים, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי מַתִּיר. מִן הָאֲשִׁישִׁים — מוּתָּר בַּעֲדָשִׁים.
segments.en: One who vows that «lentils» are forbidden «to» him «is prohibited from» eating «ashishim,» a dish made from lentils. However, «Rabbi Yosei permits» it. It is agreed by all opinions that one who vows that «ashishim» is forbidden «to» him «is permitted to» eat «lentils.»

segments.he: ״חִטָּה חִטִּין שֶׁאֲנִי טוֹעֵם״ — אָסוּר בָּהֶן בֵּין קֶמַח בֵּין הַפַּת. ״גְּרִיס גְּרִיסִין שֶׁאֲנִי טוֹעֵם״ — אָסוּר בָּהֶן בֵּין חַיִּין בֵּין מְבוּשָּׁלִין. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: ״קֻוֽנָּם גְּרִיס אוֹ חִטָּה שֶׁאֲנִי טוֹעֵם״ — מוּתָּר לָכוֹס חַיִּים.
segments.en: If one says: «Ḥitta,» wheat in singular form, or «ḥittim,» wheat in plural form, are konam for me, and for «that» reason «I» will not «taste» them, he is «prohibited from» eating wheat, «whether» as «flour or bread.» If one says: «Pounded bean» or «pounded beans» are konam for me, and for «that» reason «I» will not «taste» them, he is «prohibited from» eating «them, whether raw or cooked. Rabbi Yehuda says» that if one says: «Pounded bean or ḥitta is konam» for me, and for «that» reason «I» will not «taste» them, he is «permitted to chew» them «raw,» as that is not the normal way to eat them, and therefore was not included in the intention of the vow.
